title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page does not belong to the cycles/Hodge-index material on the neighbouring pages. It is a typed page from Grothendieck's comments on someone else's write-up (almost certainly Dieudonné's) of his draft on formally smooth algebras and Cohen's structure theorems. That material became EGA 0_IV §19. It was probably filed into cote 14 by accident.

(1) First lines. These finish a lifting argument. Given the target D' as a limit of quotients, the lift u' is the composite B → E_{k,n} → E'_{j,n} → D'. The first arrow is the transition homomorphism and the last is the already-constructed u'_{j,h}. This is the usual step showing that formal smoothness relative to discrete quotients gives liftings for complete (pro-) targets.

(2) Grothendieck asks that Corollary 2.2 be stated as an equivalence of three conditions, for an augmented situation B → C = B/I with B carrying the I-adic topology:
(i) B is 'formellement simple', the early term for formally smooth.
(ii) Conditions 1° and 2°. Presumably I/I^2 is a projective C-module, and Sym_C(I/I^2) → gr_I(B) is an isomorphism (or the analogous condition on B/I^{n}).
(iii) The completion of B is isomorphic, as a topological algebra, to the completion of B' = Sym_C(P) for a projective C-module P, with the topology given by the augmentation ideal.
He notes that (iii) is often convenient and comes out directly in the proof. A handwritten addition sketches an (iii bis): a lifting criterion 'pour tout hom de B dans D/J…'. A marginal note concerns I/I^2 being of finite type and the symmetric algebra with B_0 = C. In modern terms this is EGA 0_IV 19.5.3–19.5.4: formal smoothness of an adic augmented algebra is equivalent to its completion being a completed symmetric algebra (a formal power series algebra) over a projective module.

(3) On the 'Cohen' paragraph: 3.4 should become an immediate corollary of 3.3 via 2.2. He proposes an order for the corollaries of 3.3:
1° Existence of a coefficient field in a complete noetherian local ring when the residue field extension is separable (cf. 3.5).
2° A point 'forgotten in my draft'. For A complete noetherian local, the following are equivalent: (i) A contains a field; (ii) if char k(A) = p > 0 then pA = 0; (iii) A is a quotient of k[[T_1,…,T_n]] for some field k; (iv) when A is a domain with fraction field K, k(A) and K have the same characteristic. He says (iv) should only be a comment, to recall the old phrase 'equal characteristic case'. He recommends dropping that phrase, since 'A contains a field' is just as short and 'equal characteristic' is ambiguous for non-domains, e.g. artinian rings.

All of this is foundational editing for EGA 0_IV §19 (Cohen structure theory via formal smoothness).
errors: No mathematical errors. The equivalences in 2° are correct. If char k(A) = 0, every integer is a unit in A, so Q ⊂ A. If char k(A) = p and pA = 0, A contains F_p and Cohen's theorem gives a coefficient field. (iv) is equivalent to (ii) for domains. The lifting composite in the first lines is standard; it is shown only partially here, so it cannot be checked fully.

ideas.what: Formal smoothness of an adic augmented algebra is equivalent to (I/I^2 projective and Sym → gr an isomorphism), which is equivalent to the completion being a completed symmetric algebra of a projective module
ideas.modern_name: Structure of formally smooth adic algebras (completed symmetric algebra / formal power series)

ideas.what: Existence of coefficient fields in complete noetherian local rings with separable residue extension, derived from formal smoothness
ideas.usually_credited_to: I. S. Cohen (1946); reproved via formal smoothness in EGA

ideas.what: For a complete noetherian local ring: contains a field ⇔ (char k = p ⇒ pA = 0) ⇔ quotient of k[[T_1..T_n]]; recommendation to drop the 'equal characteristic' terminology
ideas.modern_name: Equicharacteristic complete local rings / Cohen structure theorem

ideas.what: Use of 'formellement simple' for formally smooth
ideas.modern_name: Formally smooth (early 'simple' terminology for smooth morphisms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck's early terminology (e.g. early SGA 1 drafts)

missed.claim: Archival and historical point only. This page is Grothendieck's editorial comment on the draft of EGA 0_IV §19. It shows him reorganising the Cohen corollaries and adding the 'contains a field' equivalence he had forgotten. It also documents his explicit rejection of the 'égale caractéristique' terminology. It is misfiled among the cycles/standard-conjectures notes.
missed.quote: Je suggère que nous ne suivions pas cette terminologie, car il est aussi court de dire "A contient un corps", et la terminologie "égale car" est fort ambigue pour des anneaux non intègres
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It is useful for the history of EGA's writing (the Grothendieck–Dieudonné collaboration) and for cataloguing the archive. There is no new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine editorial comments on material that appeared in EGA 0_IV §19. The only interest is archival: it shows the drafting process and a terminological choice, and the page is misfiled.
transcription_corrections: 'k T_1,...,T_n' should be k[[T_1,...,T_n]] (formal power series ring); the brackets were not typed.
'Si car k(A) = p [?] 0' should read 'car k(A) = p ≠ 0' (or p > 0).
'B form simple' means 'B formellement simple', the early term for formally smooth.
The overstruck letters before 'B' in the first line are typing deletions; the composite is B → E_{k,n} → E'_{j,n} → D' with the last arrow u'_{j,h}.
The handwritten insertion begins '(iii bis) Pour tout hom de B dans … D/J', i.e. a lifting-type criterion. The left-margin note mentions 'I/I^2 … de type fini'. The rest is largely illegible.
